title: BAIRNSDALE
tickerText: BAIRNSDALE IS THE COMMERCIAL HEART OF EAST GIPPSLAND AND A CLASSIC REGIONAL VICTORIAN TOWN WITH A STRONG CONNECTION TO THE LAND, RIVERS AND LAKES THAT SURROUND IT. SITTING ON THE MITCHELL RIVER, AROUND 280 KILOMETRES EAST OF MELBOURNE, IT’S A NATURAL GATEWAY TO THE GIPPSLAND LAKES, PAYNESVILLE, LAKES ENTRANCE AND THE WILDER COUNTRY FURTHER EAST. THE TOWN CENTRE MIXES COUNTRY PUBS, CAFES, LOCAL SHOPS AND HISTORIC BUILDINGS, WHILE THE WIDE MEDIAN STRIP ALONG MAIN STREET GIVES BAIRNSDALE ITS DISTINCTIVE COUNTRY-TOWN CHARACTER. LANDMARKS INCLUDE ST MARY’S CHURCH WITH ITS REMARKABLE INTERIOR MURALS, THE MITCHELL RIVER AND THE OLD RAILWAY PRECINCT. BAIRNSDALE SERVICES A HUGE SURROUNDING REGION, SO IT HAS THE BUSY, PRACTICAL FEEL OF A WORKING COUNTRY CENTRE RATHER THAN JUST A TOURIST TOWN. WITH WATER, FARMLAND, FORESTS AND MOUNTAINS ALL WITHIN REACH, IT’S AN IDEAL STARTING POINT FOR EXPLORING EAST GIPPSLAND.

videos.title: Bairnsdale Victoria Australia Aerial View 4K East Gippsland
videos.description:
Overview
Your ideal base for exploring the vast Gippsland Lakes, Mitchell River and the surrounding forests, Bairnsdale is a laid-back country town close to scenic drives. 
Water's edge 
The gateway to the world famous Gippsland Lakes, Bairnsdale is the perfect spot to stock up on boating, surfing, camping and fishing gear for your outdoor adventure. Choose from the wide range of shops and services on offer, and there are plenty of accommodation options available for those who would like to settle in for a few days. 

Located at the junction of the Great Alpine Road and the Princes Highway, Bairnsdale also provides easy access to the alpine villages of Omeo, Dinner Plain and Mount Hotham.

History and culture 
Tour the Bataluk Cultural Trail and discover elements of Koorie history and culture, or visit the Krowathunkooloong Keeping Place to view artefacts and history on the Gunaikurnai people of East Gippsland.

Be sure to leave time for a visit to St Mary's, an impressive Romanesque church built at the beginning of the 19th century. Wander in and check out the murals by Italian artist Francesco Floreani, which attract some 80,000 visitors to the church every year. 

Delve into the creative heart of the region at the East Gippsland Art Gallery. See works by local and visiting artists across a range of mediums, including paintings, drawings, mixed media, prints and 3D works. 

Bairnsdale is also a commercial centre for the local wool, dairy and timber industries.

Local flavours
Discover the region's wineries, brewery, restaurants and markets with many experiences located within a short drive of the town. Visit during the summer months and pick your own fruit at orchards and berry farms.

Tổng quan
Cơ sở lý tưởng của bạn để khám phá Hồ Gippsland rộng lớn, Sông Mitchell và những khu rừng xung quanh, Bairnsdale là một thị trấn nông thôn thoải mái gần những con đường lái xe ngắm cảnh.
mép nước
Cửa ngõ vào Hồ Gippsland nổi tiếng thế giới, Bairnsdale là địa điểm lý tưởng để mua sắm các thiết bị chèo thuyền, lướt sóng, cắm trại và câu cá cho chuyến phiêu lưu ngoài trời của bạn. Chọn trong số rất nhiều cửa hàng và dịch vụ được cung cấp, đồng thời có rất nhiều lựa chọn chỗ ở cho những ai muốn định cư trong vài ngày.

Nằm ở ngã ba của Đường Great Alpine và Đường cao tốc Princes, Bairnsdale cũng giúp khách dễ dàng đi đến các ngôi làng trên núi Omeo, Dinner Plain và Núi Hotham.

Lịch sử và văn hóa
Tham quan Đường mòn văn hóa Bataluk và khám phá các yếu tố của lịch sử và văn hóa Koorie, hoặc ghé thăm Nơi lưu giữ Krowathunkooloong để xem các đồ tạo tác và lịch sử của người Gunaikurnai ở Đông Gippsland.

Hãy chắc chắn dành thời gian cho chuyến viếng thăm St Mary's, một nhà thờ La Mã đầy ấn tượng được xây dựng vào đầu thế kỷ 19. Dạo quanh và xem những bức tranh tường của nghệ sĩ người Ý Francesco Floreani, thu hút khoảng 80.000 du khách đến nhà thờ mỗi năm.

Khám phá trung tâm sáng tạo của khu vực tại Phòng trưng bày Nghệ thuật East Gippsland. Xem các tác phẩm của các nghệ sĩ địa phương và các nghệ sĩ đến thăm trên nhiều phương tiện, bao gồm tranh vẽ, bản vẽ, phương tiện hỗn hợp, bản in và tác phẩm 3D.

Bairnsdale cũng là một trung tâm thương mại cho ngành công nghiệp len, bơ sữa và gỗ của địa phương.

hương vị địa phương
Khám phá các nhà máy rượu vang, nhà máy bia, nhà hàng và chợ của vùng với nhiều trải nghiệm nằm cách thị trấn một quãng lái xe ngắn. Ghé thăm trong những tháng mùa hè và hái trái cây của riêng bạn tại vườn cây ăn quả và trang trại quả mọng.

 It offers self-contained accommodation with free WiFi.
Bairnsdale Holiday Park is just a 10-minute walk from a variety of shops, cafes and a supermarket.
 Sun Cinema Bairnsdale is a 12-minute walk away.
 Lakes Entrance is a 30-minute drive away.
All accommodation is air-conditioned and features a stovetop, microwave and fridge.
 It offers a dining and lounge area with a flat-screen TV.
 Some villas have a patio with river views.
You can relax in the gardens, or enjoy a meal in the BBQ area.
 The property also features a communal kitchen, laundry facilities and a children’s playground.
 Guests can enjoy free fishing.

videos.title: Aboriginal Scarred Tree - Bark Canoe (Bairnsdale, Victoria, Australia)
videos.description:
Aboriginal Scarred Tree - Bark Canoe (Howitt Park, Bairnsdale, Victoria, Australia)

Indigenous Australians (Aboriginals) make scarred trees for creating canoes & shelters and are scattered across all regions of Australia in many different forms making them some of the most common and easiest to find archaeological sites in Australia.
Deep cuts were made in the tree with the use of various tools generally stone to remove an area of bark with parallel sides and slightly pointed or rounded ends leaving a scar in the tree.
The most common types of trees used were native Australian Eucalyptus trees such as the Box or Red Gum.
Scarred trees dating much older than 200 years can still be found around Australia. 

For more information please check out the following;
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarred_tree
http://australianmuseum.net.au/Indigenous-bark-canoe-from-New-South-Wales/
http://www.environment.nsw.gov.au/resources/cultureheritage/ScarredTreeManual.pdf

videos.title: Raining in Bairnsdale ? Victoria Australia
videos.description:
It's been raining all day, and is still as i type. More to come tomorrow also according to the forecast. It makes a pleasant change. Therapeutic even.  There hasn't been much of it in recent times.
Some local weather phenomenon chat.
Suffice to what some may think, it is still pretty dry in this area, and i mean around Bairnsdale. Can't comment on other parts of East Gippsland. From my observations, most dams are rather low. If some are full, it most probably is from a bore. Cheers!

videos.description:
Bairnsdale is a vibrant regional town located in the East Gippsland region of Victoria, Australia. Situated on the Mitchell River, it serves as a gateway to the picturesque Gippsland Lakes and the nearby high country. Known for its charming blend of history, natural beauty, and cultural attractions, Bairnsdale offers something for everyone.

The town features historic landmarks such as St. Mary's Catholic Church, renowned for its stunning murals and architecture. Visitors can enjoy the Mitchell River Walk, a scenic trail showcasing the area's rich flora and fauna. Bairnsdale's thriving arts scene is evident in its galleries, craft stores, and local markets, while its cafes and restaurants highlight fresh local produce.

As a hub for outdoor enthusiasts, Bairnsdale provides easy access to fishing, boating, hiking, and wildlife spotting. The nearby Buchan Caves and the Great Alpine Road are popular destinations for day trips. Its warm, friendly community and relaxed atmosphere make Bairnsdale an ideal stop for travelers exploring Victoria’s diverse landscapes.

channelMasterConfig.tickerText: BAIRNSDALE IS THE COMMERCIAL HEART OF EAST GIPPSLAND AND A CLASSIC REGIONAL VICTORIAN TOWN WITH A STRONG CONNECTION TO THE LAND, RIVERS AND LAKES THAT SURROUND IT. SITTING ON THE MITCHELL RIVER, AROUND 280 KILOMETRES EAST OF MELBOURNE, IT’S A NATURAL GATEWAY TO THE GIPPSLAND LAKES, PAYNESVILLE, LAKES ENTRANCE AND THE WILDER COUNTRY FURTHER EAST. THE TOWN CENTRE MIXES COUNTRY PUBS, CAFES, LOCAL SHOPS AND HISTORIC BUILDINGS, WHILE THE WIDE MEDIAN STRIP ALONG MAIN STREET GIVES BAIRNSDALE ITS DISTINCTIVE COUNTRY-TOWN CHARACTER. LANDMARKS INCLUDE ST MARY’S CHURCH WITH ITS REMARKABLE INTERIOR MURALS, THE MITCHELL RIVER AND THE OLD RAILWAY PRECINCT. BAIRNSDALE SERVICES A HUGE SURROUNDING REGION, SO IT HAS THE BUSY, PRACTICAL FEEL OF A WORKING COUNTRY CENTRE RATHER THAN JUST A TOURIST TOWN. WITH WATER, FARMLAND, FORESTS AND MOUNTAINS ALL WITHIN REACH, IT’S AN IDEAL STARTING POINT FOR EXPLORING EAST GIPPSLAND.
